paper_title: Searching for dark matter with a 1000 km baseline interferometer
coupling_convention: g_aNN in GeV^-1 (ALP-neutron gradient coupling), exactly as plotted on the y-axis of Fig. 4
notes: Paper reports new 95% CL exclusion limits from a two-station K-Rb-3He comagnetometer interferometer (Mainz-Krakow, GNOME/CASPEr family) on ALP gradient couplings to neutrons, protons, and electrons over masses 1e-22 to 4e-14 eV (frequencies 1e-8 to 11.6 Hz). Detailed limit curves are only shown in Figures 4-6 (not tabulated); the only explicit numbers in text are the best limits: gaNN < 1e-9 GeV^-1 in the mass range 1.2e-17 to 4e-17 eV (emitted here), gaPP < 1e-7 GeV^-1, gaee < 1e-6 GeV^-1. The emitted two points represent the plateau of best sensitivity for the neutron coupling; limits weaken toward both ends of the nine-decade mass range (roughly 1/f noise scaling below 0.1 Hz). Couplings are in GeV^-1 (g/f_a convention); multiply by 2*m_neutron ~ 1.88 GeV to obtain dimensionless g_an if needed. Local DM density assumed 0.4 GeV/cm^3.
